summary: Streaming chat responses disconnecting or stalling mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) for Craftlytics - increased tail latency after deploy
description:
Issue summary: Craftlytics reported that long-running streaming chat responses would either stall mid-generation (no further SSE events) or disconnect (WebSocket 1006) during tail tokens. Impact: ongoing user-facing degradation for a major customer on Dedicated capacity causing partial feature disruption and potential downstream errors in their app. Environment: prod - us-east-1, dedicated pool for Craftlytics. First observed after deploy on 2026-02-27 03:40 UTC.

Observed behavior:
- SSE connections receive initial tokens then either stall with no further data for 20-60s or terminate unexpectedly with client-side error.
- WebSocket sessions show close code 1006 on client.
- Non-streaming (batch) responses complete but with elevated latency.

Impact: Craftlytics reports ~15% of streaming sessions affected; degraded UX for chat and a spike in client reconnect attempts.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use Craftlytics account on prod (dedicated pool).
2) Start a streaming chat session that requests a long generation (~600 tokens) using rwkv-13b-8bit.
3) Observe initial tokens stream; after ~100-400 tokens either stall or connection closes unexpectedly.

Logs/Artifacts:
- Customer-provided websocket logs attached in comments.
- Server logs show repeated entries around the time of incidents: "ERROR: write tcp ...: broken pipe" and several upstream 502/504 from model-backend.
- Traces: link to perf dashboard (redwood-console): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streams/latency?from=2026-02-27&to=2026-02-28
- Canary deploy PR that went live before incident: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4128

Notes: This ticket was escalated to SRE due to customer impact and potential capacity/configuration regressions.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-27 04:10 UTC - Support triage: validated customer logs; initial hypothesis: streaming proxy closed connection due to backend stall or increased head-of-line blocking.

2026-02-27 05:00 UTC - SRE (Diego): checked autoscaler and observed reduced available worker slots in Craftlytics dedicated pool coincident with deploy traffic spike; queue times spiked to >1.2s median and tail >6s for model inference requests.

2026-02-27 06:15 UTC - Added tracing on streaming proxy and serving-runtime; found long-lived epoll waits and burst of socket write timeouts to the runtime (EPIPE / broken pipe) when the runtime experienced transient OOM'd quantized kernels.

2026-02-27 07:00 UTC - Correlated timeline with PR 4128 which introduced a kernel selection change and more aggressive sequence-based batching. Can reproduce locally under high-concurrency load where batching aggregated incompatible sequence-length requests causing memory pressure and runtime stalls.

2026-02-27 08:20 UTC - Hypothesis: new batching/kernel-selection behavior increased memory spikes for certain request combinations, causing intermittent backend stalls. Streaming proxy, which expects steady token emission, times out or closes connection when backend stalls, resulting in client disconnects or stalls.

2026-02-27 09:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation tested: forced fallback to older kernel selection and reduced max batch size for Craftlytics pool; observed immediate reduction in stalls in canary and customer environment.

2026-02-28 02:30 UTC - Verified that non-streaming endpoints also experienced higher tail latency but did not disconnect (they simply returned later). Streaming is more impacted because of timeouts and proxy behavior.
2026-03-01 12:10 UTC - Eng created PR 4152 to revert aggressive kernel-selection changes and add safety checks around batch memory accounting.

2026-03-02 03:00 UTC - Rolled back PR 4128 in production for Craftlytics dedicated pool and increased worker capacity temporarily to clear backlogs. Monitoring shows stabilized tail latency and no further streaming disconnects reported.
2026-03-03 09:00 UTC - Post-rollback monitoring: 72h window shows streaming error rate for Craftlytics down to baseline (<0.5%). Marking incident resolved pending follow-up hardening tasks.
resolution:
Root cause: a recent change to kernel selection and sequence-aware batching (PR 4128) caused transient memory pressure and runtime stalls for certain mixed-length request batches. Streaming proxy closes/timeout behavior exposed these stalls as mid-generation disconnects or stalls for SSE/WebSocket clients. Fix: rolled back PR 4128 for affected fleets, applied emergency configuration: reduced max_batch_size and increased worker pool for Craftlytics dedicated capacity, and applied additional safety checks in PR 4152.

Rollout notes: rollback applied to Craftlytics dedicated pool on 2026-03-02 03:00 UTC. Full rollback completed across us-east-1 by 2026-03-02 08:00 UTC. Monitoring dashboards show stabilized P50/P95/P99 token emission latencies.

Workarounds for customers: pin model to prior variant (rwkv-13b-8bit@v2026-02-20), disable streaming in client if acceptable, or reduce requested max tokens.

Follow-ups:
- Ensure batching memory accounting is validated under mixed-length workloads (owner: serving-runtime team).
- Add canary workload that simulates long-streaming sessions to catch regressions.
- Update streaming proxy to tolerate short backend stalls by buffering up to 10s before hard-close (owner: networking team).
